title: Security of the Aggressive RPAEF/ForkSkinny Variant
summary: The aggressive RPAEF variant introduces a reduced-round design, but its security after adjusting rounds to the effective tweak size remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Determine the security of the aggressive RPAEF variant based on ForkSkinny, which lowers the number of applied rounds to those of ForkSkinny-128-256 for all associated-data blocks and for all message blocks except the final one, because one tweakey-register component is effectively unused for those blocks. The unresolved task is to provide a thorough security analysis of this variant when its round counts are adjusted to the effective tweak size, taking into account that each tweak is used with a fixed number of rounds.

scope.domain: Cryptanalysis of an authenticated-encryption mode variant based on the ForkSkinny forkcipher.
parameters: round count, the number of applied rounds for each block type
effective tweak size, the basis for adjusting the round count
block category, distinguishing associated-data, nonfinal message, and final message blocks
tweak usage, with each tweak used for a fixed number of rounds
scope.unresolved_remainder: A thorough security analysis of the aggressive variant with round counts adjusted to the effective tweak size remains unresolved.

citations.label: Forkcipher: A New Primitive for Authenticated Encryption of Very Short Messages

progress.summary: The source presents a more aggressive RPAEF optimization using reduced rounds for associated-data and nonfinal message blocks because one tweakey-register component is effectively unused there. It explicitly leaves a thorough security analysis of the adjusted variant as an open question and notes that each tweak is used with a fixed number of rounds.
citation_labels: Elena Andreeva et al., Forkcipher: A New Primitive for Authenticated Encryption of Very Short Messages
